title: What Happens When You Get a Stitch in Your Side?
sources: Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials, 'Why Do I Sometimes Get a Side Stitch When I Run?' ('there's no single reason why side stitches occur'; theories include internal organs pulling down on the diaphragm, which 'doesn't explain why side stitches are common in swimming', and eating right before activity; one study of 965 athletes: swimmers 75%, runners 69%, horse riders 62%; usually nothing to be concerned about; relief: slow down, deep breaths, press on the spot; avoid eating about two hours before): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/why-do-i-sometimes-get-a-side-stitch-when-i-run

Morton & Callister, Sports Medicine 2015;45(1):23-35, 'Exercise-related transient abdominal pain (ETAP)' (965 participants in six sports: swimming 75%, running 69%; 'unclear why ETAP would be prevalent in swimming as this activity is not jolting'; food or drink before exercise consistently reported to evoke it; 14% reported shoulder tip pain, the referred site for the phrenic nerve, which supplies the diaphragm; 'irritation of the parietal peritoneum appears to best explain the ailment', further research needed): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4281377 (PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25178498/)

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials, 'How To Remove Plaque From Teeth' (RDH Tenika Patterson: plaque is 'soft and sticky at first, but if it's not removed within 24 hours, it hardens like cement. That's what we call tartar.'): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/how-to-remove-plaque-from-teeth

lines.text: What happens when you get a stitch in your side?
Nearly seven in ten runners get one. Who gets more, runners or swimmers?
lines.caps: NEARLY *7 IN 10 | *RUNNERS | GET *ONE | WHO GETS *MORE | *RUNNERS | OR *SWIMMERS?

lines.text: Suspect one: food. Ever jogged after a big lunch?
Suspect two: bouncing organs tugging your diaphragm.
But here's the weird part: it can hit your shoulder.
lines.caps: *BUT HERE'S | THE *WEIRD PART | IT CAN *HIT | YOUR *SHOULDER

lines.text: Suspect three: your belly's lining, rubbing and getting irritated.
No bouncing there, so maybe it's the lining.
